# Ecclesiastes Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 409r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/ECC_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** To-everything [la-kol] [there is] a-season [zeman], and-a-time [ve-et] to-every matter [le-khol chefets] under the-heavens [tachat ha-shamayim]:

**3:2** A-time to-be-born [laledet] and-a-time to-die [lamut]; a-time to-plant [lata'at] and-a-time to-uproot [la'aqor] what-is-planted [natua].

**3:3** A-time to-kill [laharog] and-a-time to-heal [lirpo]; a-time to-tear-down [lifrotz] and-a-time to-build-up [livnot].

**3:4** A-time to-weep [livkot] and-a-time to-laugh [lischok]; a-time to-mourn [sefod] and-a-time to-dance [reqod].

**3:11** The-all [ha-kol] he-has-made [asah] beautiful [yafeh] in-its-time [be-itto]; also [gam] the-eternity [ha-olam] he-has-set [natan] in-their-heart [be-libbam] — except [mi-beli] that the-man [ha-adam] cannot find-out [lo yimtsa] the-work [ha-ma'aseh] which the-God [ha-elohim] has-done [asah] from-beginning [me-rosh] to-end [ve-ad sof].

**3:19** For the-fate [miqreh] of-the-sons of-man [benei ha-adam] and-the-fate of-the-beast [ha-behemah] — one-fate [miqreh echad] [is] to-them: as-the-death [ke-mot] of-this [zeh] so [ken] the-death of-that [zeh]; and-one-spirit [ve-ruach echad] to-all; and-the-advantage [u-motar] of-the-man over the-beast [is] nothing [ayin]; for the-all [ha-kol] [is] vapor.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1-8 — "A time for everything":** 14 pairs of opposites — 28 activities encompassing the totality of human experience. Often read as comforting; in context, Qohelet's point is deterministic. These times are set; humans do not choose them.

**v.11 — "eternity in the heart":** *Ha-olam natan be-libbam* — the book's central paradox. God has placed a sense of eternity in the human heart, yet humans cannot comprehend the whole of God's work. We are wired to seek meaning we cannot fully find.

**v.19 — "one fate":** Humans and animals share the same death. This is not nihilism but observation — Qohelet refuses to assert what cannot be empirically verified.

*— EMET*
